content.title: About
content.content: Multigrain bread with raisins is a whole‑grain loaf that combines several cereals (wheat, rye, oats, barley) with added dried raisins. It has a dense crumb, a subtle sweetness, and the caramel‑like aroma of raisins.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Multigrain bread provides more fiber and micronutrients than standard white bread.
Raisins retain many of their antioxidant compounds, such as polyphenols, even after baking.
Adding dried fruit to bread dates back to ancient Mediterranean cultures.
The blend of different grains improves the amino‑acid profile, making the loaf more nutritious.
During baking, raisins can caramelize slightly, giving the crust a golden hue.

items.title: High in fiber
items.content: Fiber supports digestion, promotes satiety, and helps regulate blood sugar levels.

items.title: Source of B‑vitamins
items.content: The grains supply thiamine, niacin, and folate, which are essential for energy metabolism and nervous system health.

items.title: Contains iron and magnesium
items.content: These minerals are important for blood formation and normal muscle function.

items.title: Antioxidants from raisins
items.content: Raisins are rich in resveratrol and quercetin, which protect cells from oxidative stress.

items.title: Low glycemic index
items.content: The combination of whole grains and raisins results in a slower rise in blood glucose compared with refined breads.

items.title: Gluten allergy
items.content: The bread contains gluten, so it should be avoided by people with celiac disease or gluten sensitivity.

items.title: Sugar content
items.content: Raisins add natural sugars, which may be a concern for strict low‑sugar diets.

items.title: Caloric density
items.content: Because of the oils and dried fruit, the loaf is more calorie‑dense than plain white bread.

items.title: Phytic acid
items.content: Some grains contain phytic acid, which can reduce mineral absorption if consumed in excess.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Enjoy the bread as a snack, for sandwiches, toast, or alongside soups and salads. It pairs well with cream cheese, nut butter, or a drizzle of honey.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store the loaf in a paper bag or bread box at room temperature for up to 3‑4 days. For longer storage, freeze it in an airtight bag and thaw slices as needed.
